name: Soulside
label: Dischord
lede: They began as Lunchmeat on a split single with Dave Grohl's first band, played an illegal East Berlin show in 1989 with no guitars in the room, and split before their best record came out. Twenty-five years later they were back.

eras.title: Lunchmeat, and Dave Grohl on the flip side
eras.text: Soulside started as a high school band with a joke name, Lunchmeat, and a split 7" shared with Mission Impossible, whose drummer Dave Grohl went on to be the most famous person to come out of D.C. punk. By 1986 they had a name they meant.

years.h: Four high schoolers call their band Lunchmeat
years.p: [[Bobby Sullivan|8f4bfc0f-bed1-4cb8-8b95-9fe2a7c9ffd2]] sings, [[Scott McCloud|11e1e118-8744-45f0-9c37-dc4944541134]] plays guitar, [[Alexis Fleisig|e99216da-6570-4906-89c2-aa3622cf2174]] drums and [[Chris Thomson|e79601f0-2aa6-415c-886e-570aea8acea1]] plays bass. The band that becomes Soulside starts here.

years.h: Lunchmeat share a 7" with Dave Grohl's band
years.p: Lunchmeat and Mission Impossible split a 7" on Sammich in 1985. Grohl drummed for Mission Impossible before [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]] and Nirvana.

years.h: Summer 1986: Lunchmeat becomes Soulside
years.p: Wikipedia dates the rename to summer 1986. Asheville Stages says 1987 and No Echo implies 1985, so the date is soft.

eras.title: Ian MacKaye at the board, Temple on bass
eras.text: Soulside grew up fast in the wake of Revolution Summer, with Ian MacKaye producing. Johnny Temple's arrival on bass set the lineup that made every record that mattered.

years.h: Less Deep Inside Keeps is the first LP
years.p: Soulside's debut album comes out on Sammich with Dischord behind it, and gets the band on the road.

years.h: Chris Thomson leaves; [[Johnny Temple|d664d24a-618a-45b2-ba5e-c5c8b8e343cb]] takes the bass
years.p: Thomson goes on to front [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]]. Temple joins, and the lineup that makes every Dischord record is set.

yt: Full set at DC Space, June 7, 1988
years.h: Trigger, Dischord No. 29
years.p: Eight songs cut at Inner Ear with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing. It's the first Soulside record with a Dischord catalog number.

eras.title: Three months on the road, then the end
eras.text: In 1989 Soulside went further than almost any D.C. band of the era, playing Poland and sneaking into an East German punk show months before the Wall fell. They cut Hot Bodi-Gram at the end of the tour and broke up before it came out.

years.h: Bass goes out on Dischord before the band leaves for Europe
years.p: Dischord No. 34 pairs Bass with 103. Footage of the band playing Bass at the old 9:30 Club, August 1989, is online.

years.big: We couldn't bring guitars nor say we were playing.
q: We couldn't bring guitars nor say we were playing.
years.h: East Berlin: one illegal church show, no instruments
years.p: Soulside play one of East Berlin's illegal punk shows, held in Lutheran churches, on a three-month DIY tour that included Poland. McCloud says it was organized by DIY punks there. Per Wikipedia and Sullivan, they were the only American band to do it.
years.xp:
Getting in meant crossing at Checkpoint Charlie with no instruments and no admitting there was a gig at all. Dischord's own history singles out the Poland and East Berlin shows as what set the band apart.

McCloud told Asheville Stages the whole tour ran on friends and "very DIY promoters." The Wall came down that November. By then Soulside was already over.

years.h: Hot Bodi-Gram is cut in Holland, at the end of the road
years.p: Twelve songs at Tango Studios, with [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] producing. One is titled A Love Supreme.

years.h: Soulside break up over Sullivan's lyrics and the direction of the music
years.p: Wikipedia cites conflict over musical direction and lyrics. The split comes right after the European tour.
years.xp:
No Echo describes friction between Sullivan's politically charged lyrics and what McCloud, Temple and Fleisig wanted from the band. Asheville Stages calls it artistic differences. Sullivan told No Echo that he "really internalized" what happened and that the conflict helped him grow.

The split ran straight down the middle. McCloud, Temple and Fleisig, plus producer Eli Janney, would be Girls Against Boys within a year. Sullivan went into music and organizing.

years.h: Live in Poland, 1989

eras.title: Girls Against Boys, reggae and a single CD
eras.text: The breakup gave the 1990s underground Girls Against Boys and sent Sullivan into activism and reggae. Dischord kept the catalog alive on one CD.

years.h: Dischord gathers three records on Soon Come Happy
years.p: Dischord No. 51 puts Trigger, the Bass 7" and Hot Bodi-Gram on one Maxi CD.

years.h: Three-quarters of Soulside plus Eli Janney become [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]]
years.p: McCloud, Temple and Fleisig team up with Janney, who produced Hot Bodi-Gram. Temple later founds Akashic Books in Brooklyn.

years.h: Sullivan goes to Boston, reggae and Food Not Bombs
years.p: He forms 7 League Boots, which mixes reggae and rock, spends five years with Food Not Bombs in D.C. and Boston, and helps start D.C.'s Anarchist Black Cross chapter.

eras.title: The four get back in a room
eras.text: A documentary premiere pulled the four back together after 25 years, and it stuck. Scattered across continents, they wrote through the pandemic and made their first album since 1989.

years.cap: Soulside at the Echo, Los Angeles, November 13, 2015
years.h: The Salad Days premiere brings Soulside back on stage
years.p: Soulside play the premiere of Salad Days: A Decade of Punk in Washington, DC (1980–90). Dischord marks 2014 as the reformation.
years.xp: Sullivan told Asheville Stages the first practice back gave him chills: "it felt like the hair on the back of my neck stood straight up." He told No Echo it was special to realize "these are still great guys."

years.h: McCloud turns 50 in Prague, with Soulside playing
years.p: One show in Prague for the guitarist's birthday. European dates follow in 2019.

years.h: Sullivan publishes Revolutionary Threads
years.p: The book is subtitled Rastafari, Social Justice and Cooperative Economics. Sullivan now lives in Asheville, where he runs the French Broad Food Co-op.

years.h: This Ship is the first new Soulside in over thirty years
years.p: Dischord No. 191 backs This Ship with Madeleine Said.

years.cap: Soulside at the Markthalle, Hamburg, May 22, 2024
yt: Runner, official video by Alexis Fleisig
years.h: Zoom twice a month, then J. Robbins's Magpie Cage
years.p: A Brief Moment In The Sun (Dischord No. 192) is Soulside's first album since 1989, written across four locations and recorded by [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] in Baltimore, with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] pitching in.
years.xp:
McCloud told Asheville Stages the band set up Zoom chats on two Saturdays a month, which he called essential, to work through ideas. Sullivan told No Echo that the lockdown gave them time to "really do it right."

Dischord lists the recording as November 2021 at Magpie Cage. The album came out November 18, 2022.
